channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Efficacy of Manual Physiotherapy Techniques for Improving Cervical Range of Motion in Infants With Congenital Muscular Torticollis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of five RCTs (n=143 infants) found that manual physiotherapy techniques significantly improved cervical range of motion in infants with congenital muscular torticollis (Cohen's d = 0.90, 95% CI: 0.54 to 1.27, p < 0.001), indicating a large overall effect with low heterogeneity.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Impact of Adding Fatigue-Focused Cognitive Behavior Therapy to Supervised Pilates-Based Core Stability Training on Balance and Walking in Patients with Multiple Sclerosis: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: Adding fatigue-focused CBT to Pilates-based core stability training significantly improved balance and gait in multiple sclerosis patients, with a between-group mean difference of -0.59 in overall stability index (95% CI: -0.70 to -0.48; p < .001) and 8.22 steps/min in cadence (95% CI: 4.40 to 12.04; p < .001) after 8 weeks.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Self-guided home-based rehabilitation for upper limb motor recovery in people with stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 14 studies (8 independent cohorts) found that self-guided home-based rehabilitation for upper limb recovery in stroke patients showed no significant advantage over other interventions (SMD = 0.10, 95% CI -0.23 to 0.44), but may offer comparable functional benefits.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Interval Between Injury and Surgery Influences Knee Biomechanics During Walking in Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstructed Patients: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 studies found that ACLR patients exhibited lower peak knee flexion angle, adduction angle, and flexion moment during walking compared to controls. Delayed reconstruction (≥ 12 months) was associated with persistent sagittal plane deficits, while early surgery (within 6 months) showed fewer long-term sagittal-plane deficits but temporary frontal-plane asymmetries.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Gait variability as a predictor of fall risk in patients with stroke: A 6-month prospective cohort study with survival analysis.
item.description: A 6-month prospective cohort study of 112 stroke patients found that stride time variability (STV) at discharge was an independent predictor of post-discharge falls. Fallers had significantly higher STV, and an optimal STV cutoff of 3.40% (AUC 0.756) showed high sensitivity (88.2%) in identifying fall risk.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Selective distal upper extremity recovery following targeted dentate nucleus temporal interference stimulation in stroke-double-blind, sham-controlled randomized controlled trial with resting-state EEG
item.description: A double-blind, sham-controlled RCT (N=47) showed that 10 sessions of dentate nucleus-targeted tTIS combined with rehabilitation significantly improved FMA-UE (adjusted mean difference 3.98 points, p = 0.006) and ARAT (adjusted mean difference 2.98 points, p = 0.005) in subacute stroke patients, particularly for distal motor control (d=2.46, p<0.001), compared to sham.
item.author: J NeuroEng Rehabil

item.title: Efficacy of action observation therapy in patients with dementia or cognitive impairment: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of nine RCTs (n=348) found action observation therapy significantly improved cognitive function (SMD = 0.86, 95% CI = 0.53 to 1.19), activities of daily living (SMD = 0.67, 95% CI = 0.22 to 1.12), and naming aphasia (SMD = 0.53, 95% CI = 0.01 to 1.05) in patients with dementia or cognitive impairment.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Virtual and Augmented Reality Feedback During Robotic Gait Training Acutely Modulate Paretic Muscle Activation, Limb Loading, and Propulsion-Related Mechanics in Chronic Hemiparetic Stroke: A Randomised Crossover Trial.
item.description: A randomized crossover trial found that virtual reality (VR) and screen-based augmented reality (AR) feedback during robot-assisted gait training acutely and differentially modulated paretic muscle activation, limb loading, and propulsion-related mechanics in chronic hemiparetic stroke, with sequential combined VR + AR producing the broadest acute modulation.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Efficacy of Low-Level Laser Therapy in Patients With Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 randomized controlled trials found that low-level laser therapy (LLLT) significantly reduced pain (Hedges' g=-1.524, P <0.001) and improved grip strength (Hedges' g=0.391, P=0.002) in carpal tunnel syndrome, with pulsed mode superior for analgesia and continuous mode for grip strength, and improved SNCV (Hedges' g=0.377, P=0.016).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Effects of Different Neuromuscular Training Modalities and Doses on Lower-Limb Injury Prevention in Athletes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 27 RCTs (27,663 participants) found NMT was associated with reduced lower-limb injury risk (RR = 0.72, 95% CI 0.64–0.82), with structured and multidimensional programs showing favorable pooled estimates. However, overall certainty of evidence was very low, and dose-related findings were exploratory.
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: Body-weight support is the dominant contributor to elevated walking cost in cerebral palsy
item.description: In children with cerebral palsy (CP, N=23) and typically developing peers (TD, N=10), body-weight support significantly reduced net energetic walking cost, with a 3.5-fold greater effect in the CP group, reducing their cost by 41% to TD levels. Mediolateral stabilization had negligible energetic effects.
item.author: J NeuroEng Rehabil

item.title: Injury risk and physical therapy utilization following knee surgery in U.S. Army soldiers: a comparison of military and non-military treatment facilities.
item.description: A retrospective cohort study of 4924 US Army soldiers found that those undergoing knee surgery at non-military treatment facilities had higher subsequent injury rates (OR = 1.22, 95% CI [1.04-1.44]) and longer physical therapy duration (8.3 vs. 7.1 weeks) compared to those treated at military facilities.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Feasibility, Safety, and Preliminary Effect Estimates of an Ultrasound-Informed Hybrid Joint-Sparing Rehabilitation Strategy in Patients With Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Prospective Non-Randomized Proof-of-Concept Study.
item.description: A prospective non-randomized proof-of-concept study (n=60) found a 12-week ultrasound-informed hybrid joint-sparing rehabilitation protocol for rheumatoid arthritis to be feasible and safe, with greater pain reduction (ΔVAS: -2.88 cm vs. -0.60 cm; p < 0.001) compared to a control group, though ultrasonographic indices did not differ.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: VRCycle: A Feasibility Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating a Virtual Reality Cycling Intervention in People With Knee Osteoarthritis.
item.description: A feasibility RCT with 41 knee osteoarthritis patients found that VR-enhanced cycling was highly feasible and acceptable, with both VR and traditional cycling groups showing improvements in pain and function after 6 weeks.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Impact of Rehabilitation Initiation Timing on Safety and Efficacy in Patients With Acute Stroke and Concurrent Heart Failure.
item.description: A retrospective cohort study of 9827 acute stroke patients with heart failure found very early rehabilitation (admission day/day 1) was associated with lower in-hospital respiratory failure (RR = 0.58), lower 90-day stroke readmission (RR = 0.33), and a higher discharge Barthel Index (mean difference = 3.66) compared to delayed rehabilitation.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: From Referral to Reality: A Mixed Methods Analysis of Barriers to Pediatric Rehabilitation Service Initiation.
item.description: A mixed-methods study analyzing 8533 pediatric rehabilitation referrals found only a 42.7% service initiation rate, with parental interviews revealing complex interacting barriers including geographic availability, scheduling, communication, cost, and family priorities.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Manual techniques for headache: who delivers what and where? A systematic review of randomized controlled trials with a practice-mapping analysis.
item.description: A systematic review of 35 RCTs on manual techniques for headache found that spinal manipulation was predominant (60%) and applied mainly to tension-type (40%) and cervicogenic (29%) headaches. Practice-mapping showed technique application varied significantly by professional background, departmental setting, and geographic localization (p = 0.044, p = 0.0012, p < 0.001) rather than headache type.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Application of the ICF in the functioning assessment of children with suspected developmental coordination difficulties.
item.description: A cross-sectional study (N=208) using the ICF framework found that children with probable Developmental Coordination Disorder (p-DCD) showed lower motor skills in activities and significantly lower involvement in community participation (p = 0.016) compared to typically neurodeveloping children.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Thoracic expansion and spirometry 120 days after adding diaphragmatic manual therapy to physiotherapy in non-specific low back pain: Follow-up of a randomized controlled trial
item.description: A follow-up to an RCT (N=50) found that adding manual diaphragmatic stretching to physiotherapy for non-specific low back pain patients significantly increased inspiratory thoracic expansion at axillary (3.38 cm), xiphoid (3.52 cm), and basal (4.12 cm) levels, as well as forced vital capacity (1.57 L) and forced expiratory volume in one second (1.49 L) at 120 days (all p < 0.001).
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Integrated care for chronic musculoskeletal (MSK) disorders is promising but incomplete: a scoping review of MSK service-delivery approaches across systems
item.description: A scoping review of 97 papers identified six key themes in integrated care for chronic MSK conditions, highlighting variability in conceptualization and delivery, frequent involvement of physiotherapists (67%), but limited evidence of whole-system integration and caregiver involvement.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord
